clue.text: Flashy bird taking in a couple of unknowns

indicators.note: the bird swallows the other letters, holding them inside itself

parts.note: the jay is a noisy crow-family bird
Z is an algebraic unknown, so two of them give a pair of Zs

explanation.surface: A showy bird has swallowed a couple of mystery items.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jazzy is bright, loud and showy, the same idea as flashy.

clue.text: A lady who can be fairly trying.

definitions.text: A lady who can be fairly trying.

parts.words: A lady who can be fairly trying
parts.note: trying here means judging a case in court, and she does it fairly as a member of a panel of twelve

explanation.surface: A woman who can be rather tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fairly trying' reads as 'rather annoying'; really it is 'trying a case fairly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female member of a jury hears a trial and is expected to judge it fairly.

clue.text: Brewer's work -almost the last word in dictionaries

definitions.meaning: the chemistry of fermentation, as used in making beer

definitions.text: almost the last word in dictionaries
definitions.meaning: it comes near the very end of an English dictionary, just before a few other Z words

explanation.definitionFit: The term names the science of fermentation in brewing, and its ZY start puts it near the end of the alphabet.

clue.text: Get a drink from foyer bar

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Buy a drink at the theatre bar in the lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerba mate is a South American herbal tea, so the first word names that drink.

clue.text: Dance — or its third or fourth part

definitions.meaning: a fast ballroom dance in common time
the basic rhythm of that dance runs slow, slow, quick, quick, so the third or fourth beat is a fast step

explanation.definitionFit: The ballroom dance takes its name from its fast steps, and the third and fourth counts of its slow-slow-quick-quick pattern are exactly such steps.

clue.text: Fall silent after question I understand to be about leader of conspiracy

indicators.note: about here means jumbled around, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone stops talking after realising, when quizzed, what a plot's ringleader is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles SEE and C (the leader of 'conspiracy') into ESCE; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiesce is to become quiet or still, a rare verb related to quiescent.

clue.text: Prior to cuts in book lists

indicators.note: the short word comes before the word for cuts

parts.note: to dice is to cut into small cubes

explanation.surface: Something that happened before reductions appeared in a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabetical lists of topics at the back of a book are its indexes, also given this Latin plural.

clue.text: Discuss informally in excitement before a boxing match

indicators.note: the fight word follows the rest, which comes before it

parts.note: a kick is a thrill, as in 'for kicks'
a bout is a contest in the ring

explanation.surface: Chatting casually about a forthcoming fight, full of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick an idea about is to talk it over casually, without reaching a decision.

clue.text: Leading lady, a star in the making

indicators.note: something in the making is still being formed, so the letters are rearranged into shape

explanation.surface: A promising actress is set to become the star of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests a theatre star; here it is an empress who led Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a tsar, or an empress in her own right, was the foremost woman of Russia.

clue.text: Heard Hispanic peasant's song

indicators.note: heard means the word is listened to rather than read, a sound-alike signal

parts.note: a peon is a labourer or peasant in Spanish America

explanation.surface: Someone heard a Latin American farmhand's tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a song of praise or triumph, originally a hymn to Apollo.

clue.text: Experienced the triumph of hope over experience

definitions.text: Experienced the triumph of hope over experience

parts.words: Experienced the triumph of hope over experience
parts.note: Samuel Johnson called a second marriage the triumph of hope over experience, so someone who has gone through it has wed again

explanation.surface: Someone has lived through optimism beating hard-won wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes Dr Johnson's famous quip about a man who married again soon after an unhappy first marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's quip was about taking a second spouse, so to have lived it is to have wed once more.

clue.text: Court action about husband

indicators.note: the lawsuit word goes around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a legal action is a case

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is brought concerning someone's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' reads as one legal phrase, but 'Court' is the definition, a verb meaning to pursue.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to pursue them romantically, and chase is used in exactly that sense of pursuit.

clue.text: News group revealing Freudian technique

parts.note: word can mean news, as in 'any word from them?'
an association is an organised group or society

explanation.surface: Some media body discloses a method from psychoanalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud and his followers used the method of free responses to prompt words to reach the unconscious.

clue.text: Annual fixture to which dancers become attached

definitions.text: Annual fixture to which dancers become attached

parts.words: Annual fixture to which dancers become attached
parts.note: on May Day dancers hold ribbons tied to a tall decorated post, so they are literally attached to this yearly fixture

explanation.surface: A yearly event in the calendar that performers grow fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixture' suggests a sporting date and 'become attached' fondness; really it is a pole fixed in the ground with ribbons tied to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribboned post is set up each spring for traditional dances, and the dancers hold ribbons fastened to it.

clue.text: Shakespeare's omission from act, with no time for revision

indicators.note: letters put up for revision get reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A playwright cut something from an act because there was no time to rewrite it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare word for leaving out is found in Shakespeare, in As You Like It, so it is fairly called his.

clue.text: Tolerate food-processor

definitions.meaning: to put up with, as in 'I can't bear it'
the organ of the body that digests what we eat

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to endure something, and the noun is the digestive organ, jokingly described as a kitchen gadget.

clue.text: Cash in, yet possibly cause for his loss

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters

explanation.surface: Taking profits now might be the reason someone loses out.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' makes indecision the cause of his loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Following the proverb about hesitating, holding back in doubt is what makes him lose.

clue.text: Arresting crooner after return of Prohibition

indicators.note: the singer's name comes after the turned word
a return means the ban word is read backwards

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban
Bing Crosby was the famous American crooner

explanation.surface: A singer is being impressive in the era after alcohol was banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' looks like an adjective meaning striking; here it means catching a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean catching and detaining someone, as police do with a suspect.

clue.text: Chap entitled right individual to enter club

indicators.note: the letters go into the word for club, entering it

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A man is entitled to have a suitable person join his club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' sounds like 'having a right to'; it means holding a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary title, so he is a man with a title, ranking below a baron.

clue.text: I am in favour of an expression of disgust

indicators.note: the contraction sits in the middle of the word for favour

parts.note: grace means favour, as in 'in her good graces'
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone declares support for a show of revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am in favour of' reads as a statement of approval; 'in' is the container signal, and 'of' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look showing pain or distaste.

clue.text: Tax food and drink heartlessly — and quantities of wine

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the word for nourishment is dropped

parts.note: fuel is what keeps a body going, so food and drink are fuels

explanation.surface: Someone is taxing meals and beverages without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large tank for wine-making, and the plural of the amount it holds gives quantities of wine.

clue.text: Reformation sect avoids universal change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A Protestant group steers clear of any wholesale reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vaudois, or Waldensians, are a pre-Reformation Alpine sect that joined the Protestant Reformation.

clue.text: 'Element that's briefly socially acceptable

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol of this metal, and U also stands for upper-class, socially acceptable usage

explanation.surface: Something that is, put shortly, fit for polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' versus 'non-U' was a 1950s British label for upper-class and not upper-class language.
explanation.definitionFit: The radioactive metal's chemical symbol is U, the same letter that labels upper-class approval.

clue.text: Junior officer gets place in top ten before soldier, perhaps

indicators.note: the insect comes after the rest, the rest coming before it
the word for place sits inside the pair of words for top and ten

parts.note: first means top, as in first place
taken as the number word
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
a soldier ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: An officer joins the elite ten ahead of a fighting man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier, perhaps' is a definition by example: the soldier is a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: This rank sits just above second lieutenant and below captain, so it is a junior commissioned officer.

clue.text: Firmly maintained it's illegally arranged

definitions.meaning: held steady and unchanging, as in 'a set view'
rigged in advance, as a match or a race can be

explanation.definitionFit: The word means set firmly in place, and also rigged by cheating, as with a bent match.

clue.text: It spans a short distance with trouble? Quite the reverse

definitions.text: It spans a short distance with trouble? Quite the reverse

parts.words: It spans a short distance with trouble? Quite the reverse
parts.note: electronic messages cross vast distances with no trouble at all, the opposite of the first claim

explanation.surface: Something struggles to cover even a little ground; or rather, it does the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail carries messages across the world instantly and with little effort.

clue.text: Element in Times nobody wanted brought back

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

indicators.note: bringing back the word reverses it, reading it from the end

parts.note: none means nobody, as in 'none came'

explanation.surface: Nobody wanted something from The Times newspaper returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: This inert noble gas is a chemical element, used in some lamps.

clue.text: Nothing for a change in a holiday is leisure pursuit

indicators.note: a letter in the phrase is changed, swapped out for a different one

parts.note: taken as written
vacation is a holiday
taken as written: the letter replaced
O, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Swapping nothing in for something on holiday becomes a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing for a' means O replaces an A; the A swapped is the second letter of VACATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocation is a hobby, something pursued for pleasure beside one's main job.

clue.text: Old setter mangled birds

indicators.note: the words are crushed and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An aged gun dog has torn some birds apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old setter' is a dog, or the crossword's own compiler; really it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotterels are small plovers, wading birds of moorland and coast.

clue.text: Like some sugar? That could make one heavy

definitions.meaning: sugar can come in cubes rather than loose grains
full of clumps, like porridge or custard, which sits heavy on the stomach

explanation.definitionFit: Sugar in cubes is called lump sugar, and food full of clumps is heavy to eat.
